title: Prove exact all-role right-vector costs for small local products
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof: over a product of at most q associative local central F_q-algebras, every invertible target at every role count has exact paid right-vector cost equal to the column lower bound.

```text
R = R_1 x ... x R_k, 1 <= k <= q, n >= 1
cost_R(M) = delta_R(M) = rank_K(pi M|_{K^n}) <= n
paid factors I+u y^T, u in R^n, y in K^n
free common GL_n(K) maps anywhere; pi:R^n -> (R/K)^n
```

The new step constructs a common scalar pivot flag. Each local component excludes a proper scalar subspace, and at most q such subspaces cannot cover the row space. Apply the same choice after each Schur complement, then use the cited active-column reduction to attain delta. Residue division algebras may be noncommutative or larger than the base field; finite dimension and radical nilpotence are not assumed.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Nick Petalas #4787 for the local arbitrary-role theorem, chart reduction and explicit product question; #4601 for the two-role local-product extension; ToikY #4334 for the field-product threshold; and Nick Petalas #4243 and Wentao Li #4099 following #2513 for the alphabet and column bound. Finite-subspace counting and elimination are classical. Predecessor results are cited dependencies, not audit targets. Six files are added in one isolated package. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19213541).

## Evidence

Before, #4787 leaves arbitrary-role products open, while #4334/#4601 cover the small-product threshold at two roles. After, PROOF.md proves the all-role small-product theorem and gives an attaining factorization with no auxiliary roles.

- All 28,224 invertible three-role F2 x F2 targets pass literal matrix-word checks. Exact cost histogram at zero through three factors is `[168, 3528, 16464, 8064]`.
- A separate bit-matrix BFS enumerates all 168 normalized targets in the literal paid alphabet. All 3,696 paid edges and 28,224 free-conjugation edges satisfy its exact distance labels. Constructor costs agree throughout; 1,008 normalized basis-data actions pass.
- Another 431 distinct bounded product examples on three and four roles cover binary dual-number pairs, ternary field triples and ternary dual-number triples. All 6,644 basis-data actions and 18,200 literal scalar-subspace input checks pass. These are samples, not complete censuses.
- Eight rejection controls and two boundary fixtures pass normally and optimized. The non-coordinate fixture needs a shared scalar row combination because neither coordinate row is a unit pivot in both components.
- Both registered warning-strict commands pass locally in 2.95 s and 2.97 s, with identical generated hash-bound receipts. The package runner passes in 6.13 s. These are check durations, not performance claims. Environment is CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, standard library only.
- Committed-byte and source-history preflight passes on `c125e0765f0a28f5c3cc2e5d1d599babbcd292ed`, covering all nine package/input files and the pinned main ancestor. Official committed export and declared-input integrity pass. A read-only Git-free optimized replay with an empty PATH gives the identical receipt and preserves all ten exported files, including the exporter manifest.
- In-memory compilation, function-size inspection and staged whitespace checks pass. The longest function is 41 lines. Fixed domains bound the documented managed Python allocation deviation. Current selected source-binding orientation also passes; no selected scientific replay or predecessor suite was run.

Reproduce from the repository root with CPython 3.12:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B -W error research/right-vector-small-local-products/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -B -W error research/right-vector-small-local-products/verify.py

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/right-vector-small-local-products --check-source-history
```

The direct verifier ends with `PASS_RIGHT_VECTOR_SMALL_LOCAL_PRODUCTS binary_pairs=28224 sampled_targets=431 controls=8 no_new_kappa`. Any CPython 3.12 installation can replace the local path. SOURCES.json binds the exact predecessor documents to canonical base `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8. TASK.json explicitly changes the original interface card to this algebraic side question.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The all-field-size and all-role statement rests on the written scoped proof. Software uses base fields F2 and F3 and the stated domains; extension base fields and noncommutative products are not enumerated. Singular endpoints, more than q components at n>=3 and general semilocal matrix blocks are not classified. The cited two-role predecessors already show the component hypothesis matters; their counterexamples are not new deliverables here.

Native coefficient preparation, frames, routing, restoration, precision, stock and a complete physical supplier invoice remain unknown. No complete multiplication theorem follows. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and selected-construction scientific cold replay were outside scope and unrun. Every registered package command passed locally.

## Open next questions

- For n>=3 and more than q components, characterize which individual targets admit a common scalar flag attaining delta. Start with three specified binary three-role components; subspace avoidance alone no longer guarantees a row.
- Specify and fully price one native producer/consumer for a column replacement, including coefficient preparation, access, frames, restoration, precision and stock, before implementing a supplier.

## Related open work

- #5854 studies the same paid right-vector alphabet on singular three-generator square-zero radical targets. Its common-eigenrow obstruction and this invertible local-product pivot theorem concern disjoint endpoint domains. No shared numerical cost census is asserted.

The live same-alphabet search and open PR bodies were checked before committing. Merged #4787/#4601/#4334 are the direct predecessors. Searches covered main README terms, exact histogram/object terms, merged PRs, current handoffs and local reservation claims. The overlap snapshot covers 405 open PRs and 5,291 Discussion records with complete remote pagination; sparse local-note coverage is incomplete. These searches do not certify global novelty.

### Related open work refresh before DONE

This account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at `2026-10-27T09:07:22Z` were refreshed: #5854, #5855, #5856, #5857, #5858, #5859, #5860, #5861 and #5862. Their titles and result descriptions were read. #5854 remains the related right-vector-alphabet contribution described above; its singular target domain is disjoint from this invertible-target theorem. The other contributions concern symplectic completion, UT3 tariffs, clean involution compilation, Hermitian repair, directed-support inverse norms, header association and unitary-cycle conditioning. None supplies an overlapping target-cost census, so no additional numerical agreement or disagreement is asserted. No conflicting result was found within this refreshed set.
